title: COMPOSER sepsis alerts are associated with lower mortality at UC San Diego Health
summary: UC San Diego links COMPOSER to 17% lower sepsis mortality relative to a modeled counterfactual. The comparison was not randomized.
account: UC San Diego Health evaluated COMPOSER in two emergency departments among 6,217 adults with sepsis. The model went live on December 7, 2022, with follow-up through April 30, 2023. Post-deployment mortality was 9.49%, compared with a modeled counterfactual of 11.39%: an adjusted reduction of 1.9 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.3–3.5). Raw pre-deployment mortality was 10.3%. The estimated benefit was statistically significant at one hospital and not the other. The study used historical controls, without randomization or a concurrent untreated group.
purpose: Identify emerging sepsis so that clinical teams can assess and treat patients sooner.
system: COMPOSER deep-learning sepsis prediction and nurse alert system
developer: University of California San Diego research team

ratings.reason: Lower mortality represents lives preserved. The estimate relies on a historical model rather than randomized assignment.

ai_role.statement: COMPOSER analyzed patient data and alerted nurses to possible sepsis. Nurses reviewed patients with physicians, who selected treatment. The outcome concerns AI-assisted clinical care.

evidence.citation: Boussina A, Shashikumar SP, Malhotra A, et al. (2024). npj Digital Medicine 7:14. doi:10.1038/s41746-023-00986-6. Evaluation by COMPOSER's developers and deploying health system.
evidence.title: Impact of a deep learning sepsis prediction model on quality of care and survival

evidence.citation: Vazquez J. UC San Diego, January 23, 2024. Institutional account of the deployment and its clinical workflow.
evidence.title: Study: AI Surveillance Tool Successfully Helps to Predict Sepsis, Saves Lives

produced_by: Continuous analysis of electronic patient data and alerts delivered to nursing staff.
Nurse review, physician assessment, and treatment at UC San Diego Medical Center and Jacobs Medical Center.
must_hold: Reliable data and prompt clinical assessment are likely requirements. Local evaluation is needed to establish whether the benefit recurs.

headline: COMPOSER sepsis alerts are linked to lower mortality

comparator.against: Modeled post-deployment mortality without COMPOSER, using historical data and adjustment for confounders
comparator.quote: the expected counterfactual mortality rate would have been 11.39% with a 95% confidence interval of [9.79%, 13.00%]

claim_basis: Sources: the makers' peer-reviewed study and the deployer's press release. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
